Let $(A_n)_n$ be a sequence of measurable sets such that $\mu(A_n) \to 0$. Determine whether it is true that $\int_X f_n 1_{A_n} \, d\mu \to 0$. Provide a justification for your answer.

answer_text:
Yes. Assume the standard meaning of “dominated”: there exists \(g\in L^1(\mu)\) with
\[
|f_n|\le g \quad \text{a.e. for all }n.
\]
Then for every \(n\),
\[
\left|\int_X f_n \mathbf 1_{A_n}\,d\mu\right|
\le \int_{A_n} |f_n|\,d\mu
\le \int_{A_n} g\,d\mu.
\]

Since \(g\in L^1(\mu)\), the integral is absolutely continuous with respect to \(\mu\): for every \(\varepsilon>0\), there is \(\delta>0\) such that if \(\mu(E)<\delta\), then \(\int_E g\,d\mu<\varepsilon\). Because \(\mu(A_n)\to 0\), for all large \(n\), \(\mu(A_n)<\delta\), hence
\[
\left|\int_X f_n \mathbf 1_{A_n}\,d\mu\right|<\varepsilon.
\]

Therefore,
\[
\int_X f_n \mathbf 1_{A_n}\,d\mu \to 0.
\]

\[
\boxed{\text{True, the limit is }0}
\]
